text: Gold fell about 2.6% to near $3,626 in late US trading, dropping below $3,650 for the first time since September 2025 as bets on more Fed rate hikes and a firm dollar weighed.
Silver dropped about 4.4% to near $42.96, with most of the fall late in the day, pushing the gold/silver ratio up to about 84.4.
Gold miners fell with the metals: GDX closed down 3.77% at $72.00 and the 3x GDXU about 12%.
The Nasdaq fell 2.25% and the S&P 500 2.02%, its sixth straight loss, while the Dow lost 1,101 points to close below 50,000.
Anthropic opened 34% above its IPO price on its first trading day but finished up about 17%, as other AI and chip stocks slid.
The VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, jumped about 16% to 28.44 from 24.56 on Wednesday.
Brent crude settled almost flat at $91.98 a barrel, as Hormuz tanker disruptions offset worries about a supply surplus.
The dollar held near a 19-month high and the yen stayed just under 160 per dollar as AI worries cut appetite for risk.
